items.text: Claude GitHub App installed on ck5o4/multifamily with write access - cloud push unblocked
items.why: FIXED 2026-08-17 by Anthony. Root cause was subtler than 'a missing scope': the Claude app was AUTHORIZED on ck5o4 but INSTALLED only on the flux-brain-hq org, never on the personal account that owns multifamily. Authorization is what let cloud sessions read; installation is what grants repo Contents:write, so every push 403'd while every read succeeded - exactly the observed asymmetry. Installed via github.com/apps/claude/installations/new -> ck5o4 -> Only select repositories -> multifamily. Verified at installation 154488689: 'Read and write access to ... code' and 'Selected 1 repository: ck5o4/multifamily'. Scoped to that one repo deliberately. NOTE: the post-install redirect lands on claude.ai/admin-settings/... which shows 'You don't have access to organization settings' on a personal plan - that dead end is cosmetic, not a failure. CONFIRMED 2026-08-18 PM: the scheduled cloud sweep pushed to origin/main for real (3254356..feb4e3a). No 403, no recovery-patch email. TRAP FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: the cloud container starts on a DETACHED HEAD with the local 'main' ref left at a stale commit, so 'git push -u origin main' fails with 'behind its remote' and reads exactly like the old permissions failure. It is not. Fix is 'git branch -f main HEAD && git checkout main' before pushing, or push HEAD:main. SECOND HALF OF THE TRAP, found 2026-08-18: the stale ref is not just local 'main' - the remote-tracking ref 'origin/main' is ALSO stale on container start. This run opened with 'git log origin/main..HEAD' listing 9 commits that looked unpushed (including work already confirmed pushed on 08-18 PM). They were not unpushed; the container's cached origin/main simply predated them. A single 'git fetch origin main' moved origin/main ccdf19f..f38b13b and the list went empty. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUTINE: step 4 tells the scan to judge the git-push-rule todo by whether 'git log origin/main..HEAD' is empty, so ALWAYS fetch before running that test - otherwise a clean repo reads as 9 commits of lost work and the scan will 'recover' work that was never lost.

items.text: Deal Flow sweep fires 2x/day by design (cron 0 13,23) - decide the cadence; there is no duplicate routine
items.why: Found 2026-09-06; escalated 2026-09-07 (now THREE fires in one day). Two runs swept the identical window today: one at ~12:00 UTC that created digest draft r5771603367285783142 at 13:10:44Z, and a second at ~13:10 UTC that found the draft already there. Same pattern on 09-02 and 09-04, each of which has TWO unsent drafts titled 'Deal Flow digest - <date> (PM)'. Cost is not just duplicate drafts: the 12:00 run's digest carried two false statements that the second run had to repair - it claimed all digests since ~Aug 18 had empty bodies (false, every one is 2,008-4,925 chars) and it told Anthony to write a Rider reply from scratch, supplying suggested text, when draft r1750751368094010186 has held substantively that same reply since 2026-08-18. That is the 'verify before instructing' rule failing inside the routine itself. Fix: list the account's Routines, keep one Deal Flow sweep, delete the duplicate. UPDATE 2026-09-07 23:15 UTC: three fires today, not two - 00:09 (AM digest r-3531512889927791335), 13:23 (PM digest r-8315775485061088736) and 23:11. The 23:11 run repaired the 13:23 draft rather than duplicating it, and had to undo the same class of defect as on 09-06: the 13:23 digest told Anthony to 'find the correct broker contact' for Beau Box when bgarrett@beaubox.com was found 2026-08-17 and draft r5125392449427038899 has been ready since 2026-08-09, it omitted the Rider reply (r1750751368094010186, unsent 20 days) and the Hernandez request (r6910164296570484338, never sent) entirely, and it inverted the Vercher silence - Vercher answered 2026-08-03, the 35 days of silence are Anthony's. Second consecutive day an extra firing produced false instructions a later run had to repair. This is now a correctness problem, not a tidiness one. CORRECTED 2026-09-08 13:20 UTC (email sweep) - THE PREMISE OF THIS ITEM WAS WRONG. This run listed the account's Routines directly instead of inferring from draft timestamps. There is exactly ONE Deal Flow sweep routine: trig_01HJCstYwuekG3WoFodSwAQB, 'Deal Flow email sweep + board update', cron '0 13,23 * * *', enabled, created 2026-08-09, never updated since. has_more=false; the only other routines on the account are the weekly bug sweep (0 3 * * 1) and the daily scan (0 14 * * *). So TWO fires per day is the configured schedule, not a duplicate, and the fix recorded here for three days - 'list the account's Routines, keep one, delete the duplicate' - is not actionable because there is no duplicate to delete. Anthony would have gone looking for a second routine and found nothing. That is this repo's own 'verify before instructing' rule failing inside a todo, which is the same defect class the item was created to track. WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED: the ~00:09 UTC digest drafts on 09-07 (r-3531512889927791335) and 09-08 (r-5393488354865663425) match neither cron hour. Most likely they are the 23:0x fire running long and creating its draft after midnight UTC, but this run could not prove that and is not asserting it. The 13:23/13:17 and 23:11 fires are simply the schedule. WHAT TO ACTUALLY DECIDE: two sweeps a day is a cadence choice, not a bug. It is only harmful when a run with no new mail invents urgency, which is what happened 09-06 and 09-07. The prompt already guards this ('No signal = no draft') and the guard held on both fires today - the 00:09 AM digest was accurate and this 13:17 run added no duplicate. If Anthony wants one sweep a day, change the cron to '0 13 * * *' on the trigger above; an unattended run should not halve his inbox coverage on its own, so that stays his call. Reclassified from 'de-duplicate it' to 'decide the cadence'. NEW EVIDENCE 2026-09-11 13:1x UTC (email sweep), and it closes the 'unexplained ~00:09 draft' question above: the 2026-09-10 PM fire produced TWO digest drafts 55 minutes apart - r7426230499633812158 at 23:15:08Z (subject 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-10 (PM)', 5,013 chars, recipient ridgebackpeak@gmail.com) and r2145619574996706100 at 2026-09-11T00:10:20Z (subject 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-11 (PM)', 5,629 chars). Both cover the identical window and the identical three CHECK listings (Olympia, Kabel, E Boyd), so this IS the 23:00 fire running long and writing its draft after UTC midnight - exactly the hypothesis this item declined to assert on 09-08, now supported by two drafts from one fire. TWO NEW DEFECTS IN THAT LATE DRAFT, both found and fixed this run: (1) it had NO RECIPIENT AT ALL - toRecipients was absent, so the digest could not be sent, only read in the Drafts folder; (2) because UTC had rolled over, it was titled '2026-09-11 (PM)', which is TODAY's date - a digest labelled for a day it does not cover, sitting in the folder before today's sweep ran, is a trap: it invites a later run or Anthony to believe the 09-11 PM sweep already happened. Fixed by adding the recipient and retitling to 'Deal Flow digest - 2026-09-10 (PM, full triage)'. The BODY WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED - update_draft merge semantics preserve an omitted body, and this repo has already recorded two separate incidents of a body rewrite introducing a worse defect than the one it fixed, so only 'to' and 'subject' were passed. Its first body line still reads '2026-09-11 (PM)'; that is known and left alone on purpose. NOTE the draft-count cost is now visible: FOUR digest drafts exist for 2026-09-10 alone (13:19, 13:23, 23:15, 00:10). STANDING CHECK FOR FUTURE SWEEPS: after creating a digest draft, re-read it and confirm toRecipients is populated - a digest with no recipient reads as a normal draft in every listing that omits the recipient field, which is how this one survived a full day unnoticed. Cadence decision itself is still Anthony's and still unmade.

items.text: SCREEN 312/314/316 Farrar Ave, Kenner LA 70062 (Jefferson) - 3 detached houses sold as one package, $402,300 ask ($134,100/unit). Needs VERIFIED rents/leases before any offer.
items.why: NEW 2026-09-09 AM (email sweep), from a Crexi saved-search alert 2026-09-08 19:57 UTC. This is the only listing in the 09-08/09-09 batch that is inside NEGOTIATING distance of the house gates rather than an order-of-magnitude miss, which is why it gets its own item instead of being parked in nola-listing-pull. Crexi labels it 'Multifamily | 3 Units | $134,100/unit'; a web search shows 312 Farrar Ave on its own as an ACTIVE single-family listing (MLS 2561548, 3bd/2ba, ~1,503 SF, ~$168,900), so the Crexi listing is an ASSEMBLAGE of three adjacent detached houses, i.e. a small SFR portfolio - explicitly inside the 2026-08-02 strategy ('MHPs plus SFR/duplex portfolios'). HAND SCREEN, ESTIMATED BASIS, STATED AS SUCH: Kenner 70062 3BR house rents run $1,400-2,000 with the single-family median ~$1,850; at a deliberately conservative $1,600/mo x 3 = $57,600 GPR, 7pct vacancy, Jefferson insurance $3,000/unit wind, Jefferson millage 118.40, mgmt 9pct, and the CLAUDE.md per-unit expense lines with utilities tenant-paid, NOI is ~$29.7K at ask = 7.38pct cap, and DSCR at 75pct LTV / ~7pct / 25yr is 1.147 - UNDER the 1.30 house floor. The price clearing 1.30 DSCR is ~$361K, a 10pct cut from ask. Compare the rest of the pipeline: Baker needed 37pct off, Eden 26pct, Hwy42 17pct plus heavy carry, Kabel Dr 68pct. A 10pct cut is a conversation, not a fantasy. DO NOT OVERREAD THIS: 1.30 DSCR is a FINANCING gate, NOT the house rule. Whether ~$361K also clears the 13pct IRR / beats-the-index band has NOT been run and needs the real solver on verified rents. Open items before any offer, in order: (1) actual leases or a rent roll - the $1,600 is a market estimate off listing sites, which is exactly the Treme trap; (2) bindable Jefferson wind insurance quote - $3,000/unit is assumed, and per the 2026-08-17 metro/inland finding the insurance quote, not capital, is what binds metro deals at this size; (3) run flood.py - Kenner is Jefferson and much of it sits behind levees; (4) condition/vintage on all three houses (vintage capex was the bug that killed Baker and Treme on re-screen); (5) the management-economics caveat from CLAUDE.md applies hard here - 3 SCATTERED DETACHED doors is the thinnest possible third-party-management profile, worse than 3 units in one building, and per-deal closing/loan/insurance minimums spread over only 3 doors. Equity at ask is ~$100K, well inside the $300K capital, so capital does NOT bind.

Most likely reading: the listing is a PORTION of the Kabel Estates complex (two buildings) marketed under the complex's name. That is an inference, not a fact.

HAND SCREEN, ESTIMATED BASIS, STATED AS SUCH. House Orleans overlay per CLAUDE.md (7.5pct vacancy+bad debt, Orleans millage 131.99 via latax.py = $5,266 at ask, insurance $3,000/unit wind, mgmt 8pct of EGI, G&A/mktg/R&M/other/utilities per unit, payroll $0 under 20 units) at the repo default 6.75pct / 25yr / 75pct LTV.   With vintage capex ACTIVE (1965 = 61 years = the 40+ band, $750/unit, per tools/fitted_params.json) - the correct treatment, and the exact adjustment that killed Baker and Treme on re-screen:
    8 units @ $900: NOI $23,633, cap 5.92pct, DSCR at ask 0.953, clears 1.30 at $307K (-23pct)
    8 units @ $950: NOI $27,718, cap 6.95pct, DSCR at ask 1.117, clears 1.30 at $351K (-12pct)

VERDICT: SCREEN-WORTHY, not yet actionable. On the central case (8 units, $950 rents, vintage capex) the 1.30 DSCR price is ~$351K against a $399K ask - a 12pct cut. That is a conversation, not a fantasy: compare Baker 37pct, Eden 26pct, Hwy42 17pct, 3260 Kabel 68pct, Farrar Kenner 10pct. DO NOT OVERREAD IT. 1.30 DSCR is a FINANCING gate, NOT the house rule - whether ~$351K also clears 13pct IRR / beats the index has NOT been run and cannot be until the unit count and rents are real. The $45/SF ask is unexplained and the three plausible explanations (major condition problem, heavy vacancy, or a partial-interest/portion sale) are all material.

OPEN ITEMS BEFORE ANY OFFER, IN ORDER: (1) UNIT COUNT AND WHAT THE $399K ACTUALLY BUYS - which buildings of the complex, how many doors; one call to the listing broker or the LoopNet page settles it and nothing else can proceed without it; (2) actual leases or a rent roll - $925-975 is advertised, not contracted; (3) condition/capex on a 1965 building - roof and HVAC ages, and why it is priced at $45/SF; (4) bindable Orleans wind insurance quote - $3,000/unit is ASSUMED, and per the 2026-08-17 metro/inland finding the quote, not capital, is what binds metro deals at this size (this is the same gate apartment-guard has been sitting on since 08-05); (5) flood - flood.py could NOT run this sweep (curl exit 56, the standing network-policy block), so the flood zone is UNVERIFIED. Equity at ask is ~$100K plus closing, well inside the $300K capital, so capital does NOT bind.
